Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating Emily Stone, an 8-year-old girl in the third grade who presents for comprehensive assessment. She takes only a daily multivitamin, has met all developmental milestones, and has a noncontributory family history. 

Emily’s height tracks steadily along the 50th percentile, showing neither excessive tallness nor stunted growth. Craniofacial examination shows a normal head shape without elongation, preserved malar fullness, and eyes that are not sunken or deep-set. Intraoral inspection reveals a vaulted, steep hard palate accompanied by significant crowding of her dentition. A formal ophthalmology evaluation noted significant nearsightedness and bilateral superior displacement of the crystalline lenses; importantly, there was no lens notch or defect, and the neurosensory retinae remain fully attached.

On musculoskeletal review, she exhibits remarkably slender, elongated fingers and toes, along with widespread articular hypermobility, though full extension of both elbows is preserved. Her feet demonstrate pronounced flattening of both plantar arches. Her spine shows no lateral curvature, and her chest wall lacks any inward depression or outward sternal protrusion. The skin displays normal pliability without cutaneous stiffness or stretch marks, and the groin regions are entirely free of herniation.

A recent echocardiogram identified distinct aneurysmal enlargement of the sinuses of Valsalva as well as systolic billowing of the mitral leaflets. Reassuringly, there was no mitral backflow, and no intimal tear or dissection flap was visualized along the ascending aorta.

I would be grateful for your expert clinical opinion and management recommendations for Emily.

Sincerely,

Dr. Marcus Vance
